answer: Persistent Attention Ledger. Each identity must maintain a public stream of time-stamped, task-linked work that decays unless refreshed; agents earn standing only through continuous genuine activity, and a willow-thin history gets filtered out. Duplicates can't share one stream without colliding on schedule and content, creating a ripple of detectable overlap. Aggregate standing is capped at the median so farms gain no zenith advantage. An attacker running N sock puppets pays N full attention budgets—real compute and operator hours—so scaling identities scales cost linearly, not once.
